waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Same pullout used for the Kangaroo Temple/West Route approach on the outside of the SR-20 hairpin; no permit required.
waypoints.directions: Park in the pullout at the hairpin turn on SR-20, a short distance east of Washington Pass at around 5,100 feet — the same roadside pullout used for the nearby West Route approach on Kangaroo Temple. No permit is required to park or climb from here.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek (West Face turnoff)
waypoints.note: The West Face line crosses the creek near here; for the south face, stay on the climbers' trail on the west side of the creek and keep heading up-valley.

waypoints.name: Kangaroo Pass
waypoints.note: Sparsely cairned bootpath tops out at 6,671-ft Kangaroo Pass, where the Beckey-Tate approach breaks east toward the south-face basin.

waypoints.name: Half Moon–Big Kangaroo Col
waypoints.note: Broad, scree-covered col centered between Half Moon and Big Kangaroo — stay centered, as the col adjacent to Half Moon is steeper and looser.
waypoints.directions: Cut left (east) from the pass toward the low point on the ridge between Big Kangaroo and Half Moon, working through the head-of-basin talus and boulder fields — this is the slow, route-finding part of the approach.

waypoints.name: Base of South Face / Runout Chimneys
waypoints.note: Low-5th ramp gives way to runout, burly chimneys (5.8+ on pitch 4) before the 900-ft south face's 5.9 finger-crack crux on pitch 5.
waypoints.directions: The col drops and traverses you into the south-facing basin directly below Big Kangaroo's south wall; expect snow lingering in the basin in early season. The line is the obvious central ramp-and-ledge system splitting the middle of the face — Kearney-Thomas takes the left fork of the prominent gully system, and Going Down Under starts here before traversing right across the overlaps.

waypoints.name: Top of South Face / Snow Gully Exit
waypoints.note: South face ends a few hundred feet below the true summit; exit up the snow-filled gully shared with the West Route to reach the summit block.
waypoints.directions: Climb the six pitches up the central ramp system: a 5.4 ramp, a burly, slightly runout 5.7 chimney, a 5.6 ramp-and-corner to a tree belay, a sustained 5.8+ chimney whose big cams sit far back in the crack, the 5.9+ finger-crack crux, and a 5.8 hand crack/corner that tops out a few hundred feet below the true summit.

waypoints.name: Big Kangaroo Summit
waypoints.note: Final 20-ft exposed, unprotected slab move tops out at the small summit bolt shared with the Southwest Rib/West Route.
waypoints.directions: From the last belay scramble about 20 ft up and left to the notch between the south face and the true summit, which stands a few hundred feet higher. To tag it, drop about 150 ft of scree on the far side, cross north into the West Route gully and climb its short pitches, finishing with the exposed, essentially unprotected 5.6 slab move past a single old 1/4-inch bolt.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Large pullout on the outside of the SR-20 hairpin switchback ~0.9 mi east of Washington Pass; no permit required to park.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the Hairpin Turn pullout, about a mile east of Washington Pass near milepost 163, at roughly 5,100 to 5,160 feet — a large pullout on the outside of the hairpin switchback. No permit is required to park.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek Crossing
waypoints.note: Easy crossing of Early Winters Creek, where the west-face line leaves the cairned climbers' trail and heads east toward the west-face gullies.

waypoints.name: Talus Fork / Gully Base
waypoints.note: Trail opens into talus and scree here; bear into the west-face approach gully.

waypoints.name: Chockstone / Loose Gully Band
waypoints.note: Chockstone marks the start of the technical climbing; the gully above is loose with a cliff band — helmet essential for rockfall.

waypoints.name: Ridge Crest Notch below Summit Block
waypoints.note: The first roped pitch, started below the chockstone, reaches the ridge crest at this notch; the second pitch traverses from here around the summit block.

waypoints.name: Big Kangaroo Summit
waypoints.note: Small, mostly unprotectable exposed 5.6 slab summit with a single old rusty bolt — room for only one climber at a time.

waypoints.name: South Face base area (shared with Beckey-Tate)
SR 20 / State Creek Pullout
waypoints.note: Same unsigned SR 20 pullout used for the South Buttress, ~1.5 mi west of Washington Pass (~0.5 mi west of the Blue Lake trailhead).
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the broad shoulder about half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead — roughly a mile and a half west of Washington Pass — where there is room to park and a view through the trees to the peak. It is unsigned and sits near 5,050 ft, so measure from Blue Lake rather than looking for a marker. If you are meeting partners, the usual arrangement is to gather at the Blue Lake lot and then drive the short distance west to this pullout.

waypoints.name: State Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Cross State Creek in the forest below the pullout before climbing into the meadows/basin southwest of the summit.

waypoints.name: Basin below Whistler Mountain
waypoints.note: Trail runs along the north side of the drainage and flattens through the open basin around 6200 ft before angling up toward Cutthroat's southwest side.

waypoints.name: Southwest Gully entrance
waypoints.note: Talus/scree/sand gully gaining the ridge; in poor visibility parties have mistaken this for the steeper, harder Second Southwest Gully just to the right.

waypoints.name: Crux face above rap station
waypoints.note: A short 5.2 face above a double-bolt belay/rappel anchor leads to easy ledges below the ridge crest; rock is loose in spots.

waypoints.name: West Ridge crest / notch
waypoints.note: Gain the ridge crest here at a notch giving access toward the north ridge; narrow, exposed catwalk over a series of crestline horns.

waypoints.name: Northwest face traverse (Northwest Ledge)
waypoints.note: Exposed, near-two-rope-length traverse across the northwest face on the ledge finish to reach the north ridge below the summit block.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak summit
waypoints.note: Final low-5th-class pitch/scramble tops out on the blocky true summit; reverse the ridge with downclimbing and short rappels to descend.
